composition.story: Deep rock melts into magma, which is lighter than the rock around it and rises into a chamber. As it rises, pressure drops and dissolved gas forms bubbles. Gas pressure grows until it is stronger than the rock cap. The cap breaks, and the gas-filled magma blasts out of the vent.

aha.observation: A volcano erupts when gas pressure in the magma becomes stronger than the rock holding it down.

parts.presentation: Top rail with short step labels; it also shows progress.

Pinned to the highlighted region to show where the change happens.
A single comparison line: gas pressure against rock-cap strength, given in words with no numbers.

states.label: Rock melts
states.sentence: Deep underground, heat melts rock into magma, which is lighter than the solid rock around it.

readouts.label: Gas pressure vs. rock cap
readouts.value: Gas still dissolved; cap holds easily

states.label: Magma rises
states.sentence: Magma rises and collects in a chamber under the volcano.
states.why: Magma floats up because it is lighter.

states.label: Gas bubbles form
states.sentence: Near the surface, pressure drops, so dissolved gas comes out as bubbles, like opening a soda.
states.why: Bubbles take up much more space than dissolved gas.

states.label: Pressure beats rock
states.sentence: Gas pressure is now stronger than the rock cap holding it down. The cap cracks.
states.why: This is the tipping point: push exceeds hold.

states.label: Eruption
states.sentence: Expanding gas pushes magma up the conduit and out of the vent as lava, ash and gas.
states.why: Released gas expands quickly and carries magma out.
